dedupe_keys.name: era common safety indicators csis eu railway accidents precursors and technical failures 2006 2024

description: The Common Safety Indicators (CSIs) are the harmonised statistics on railway accidents, precursors to accidents and technical failures that every EU Member State reports under Annex I of the Railway Safety Directive (EU) 2016/798. The European Union Agency for Railways (ERA) collects them from the national safety authorities and publishes the dataset and the reports built on it. Coverage: the EU railway system, with data from 2006 to 2024 in the latest release (updated 14 January 2026); indicators cover accidents, precursors and technical failures as defined in ERA's implementation guidance. Format and access: one XLSX file of about 1.1 MB downloadable from the ERA CSI page, with a brief guide for national reporting, implementation guidance, a data quality task force report, and main outputs such as the Report on Railway Safety and Interoperability 2026, the Annual Safety Overview 2025 and the assessment of safety targets; free. Licence: not stated on the page read. Caveats: ERAIL, the former accident information database, has been disconnected, so CSI reporting now follows new arrangements, and accident investigation reports are handled on a separate page; data quality varies between countries, which is why a task force on data quality was set up in 2023; the spreadsheet itself was not opened. Simulation uses: accident and failure rates for rail safety risk models, resilience and emergency response planning, and hazard exposure of level crossings and rolling stock. Related records: the ERA RINF register (data-era-rinf) describes the infrastructure, and the Carmont derailment investigation (case_study-carmont-passenger-train-derailment-of-12-august-2020-raib-investigation) is an example accident behind such statistics.
